angle: FOUNDATION-FIRST: tokens and test spine first (B1), then the shared bars and account (B2), the workspace shell and kit variants (B3), then screen by screen on top of them. Dead-code.unit makes an unreferenced primitive fail, so a primitive lands with its first consumer: tokens/kit variants/bars in B1-B3, the editor dock with the editor frame (B5), the overlay Drawer with the job drawer (B11).
principles: Parity rule first: UI only, every live function stays; new capabilities are PARKED. Ownership is by area file plus ID range; the CATCH-ALL rule per area (written in the owning batch) is: editor-content -> B6, editor-design-templates -> B7, editor-letter-ats-export -> B9, shell-docs -> B4, applications -> B11, projects -> B13, mobile -> B14. Every other row of a file, including any row added by review or later, belongs to that batch. Cite rows as '<file>: <ID>' (EDIT-/NEW- exist in two files; 'D-nn' is the DRAWN BUT NOT table of shell-docs, projects and mobile; 'Nn' is applications section 2).

The parity file's Fix column is the build spec and the live app wins where board and app differ. The lead turns each batch's rows (ID, live behaviour, status, fix) into docs/tracking/ui-redesign/batches/B<n>.md with a generator script (tools/brief.mjs, written in B1) so builders read the fix inline, never only the board; every CHANGED row is marked DO NOT BUILD AS DRAWN.

The phone is built with its surface, not in a phone batch: each batch owns the desktop and phone rows of its screens (mobile.md is split by section across B2-B13). Breakpoints: 768 px (editor, useIsMobile) and Tailwind sm/md/lg; the 768-1100 px band has no board and gets one rule in B5 (dock overlays below 1100) verified in B14.

Start-up path has about 0 kB spare (71-startup-chunks, cap 1,100 kB of minified JS; CSS and index.html are free). B1 creates headroom FIRST (lazy NewLetterModal+Dialog closure, lazy CareerHistoryPanel; reserve: lazy jsonResumeImport with a 122 update). Only B2 and B4 add start-up JS and each keeps a bytes ledger (71 diagnostic read before and after, in the report). B3 and B5-B13 are lazy-only. Rules for all: never import the ui barrel from start-up code; AppBar, BottomTabBar and AuthBar import only compose and named lucide icons; no new util imported by both Dashboard and a lazy chunk (it is hoisted); repeated class strings become index.css component classes.

Single-owner files, one batch at a time (batches never overlap): Editor.jsx, EditorHeader.jsx, useEditorTab.js, EditorPreviewPane.jsx, EditorTabContent.jsx = B5 only (B7-B9 plug in through DesignDock.jsx, AtsDock.jsx and the panels, which B5 creates as thin wrappers); DesignPanel*.jsx + tests/pdf/parity registries = B7; PersonalInfoEditor*.jsx, SectionEditor*.jsx, RichTextEditor.jsx, EditorResumeTab.jsx = B6; AuthBar.jsx = B2; Dashboard.jsx, ResumeCard.jsx = B1 (testid, lazy boundaries), B2 (header), B4 (body); AppRoutes.jsx = B3 and only if a route changes (expected untouched); index.css = B1, then in each later batch exactly ONE named cluster may append component classes. Inside a batch no two clusters own the same file.

Tests: no test runs here; CI only. Per batch: failfirst for every src commit's new tests, ONE combined targeted dispatch (tests + named playwright/cypress specs + 71-startup-chunks when a non-lazy file was touched), then ONE full gate on the final head. New tests assert reachability and behaviour (opener found by role+name, control inside data-testid region, same write as before, union of controls of regrouped panels equals the old walk count, negative twin for the old path), never Tailwind classes; the 56 dph/dvis class-pin files are restated as the defect they guard, with evidence, never weakened. A commit must carry its src change and its test (a tests-only commit cannot be failfirst'ed). Testid spine and per-runner helpers (openDesign, openAts, switchTo) land in B1 so B5 changes helper bodies, not 40 specs.

Protocol refinements (no step dropped): step 1 adds brief generation and, for B2/B4, a start-up read (dispatch tests: 71-startup-chunks alone, read the '# start-up path' line); step 3 render check compares against the named board for look and against tokens where no board exists (about 40% of surfaces are undrawn); step 4 reviewers check every CHANGED row with a negative twin; step 5 adds a label sweep (tools/label-inventory.mjs lists title/aria-label/placeholder/button text of touched files at base vs head; any difference must map to a parity row or be reverted; this catches the tooltip-level rows two reviewers still call unlisted); step 7 also updates docs/knowledge/*.md paths (knowledge-docs.unit) and writes a row ledger (parity ID -> test name).

Windows: each batch is sized to one 3 h window; if the gate is not reached the batch spans the next window (RUN-STATE) and nothing else starts. Likely spill: B4, B5, B6, B7, B13; each has a named split point in its risks. Nothing is pushed to master; the head after each batch is functionally complete but visually mixed, so deploy is the owner's call after B14.

Accessibility is deferred: noted in the batch reports, never planned or fixed. Commits are authored sairamgudiputi <sairamgudiputi8@gmail.com>, no trailers, no mention of Claude or AI; work goes to claude/wonderful-maxwell-vu8xqw only.

canvasCorrections.whenAndHow: No redraw before or during the build. Reasons: of the first 890 audited rows 37% are MISSING because the canvas never drew a home (undrawn panes: Design Template/Type/Spacing/Headings/More, 10 of 11 entry forms, ATS categories, every menu body, phone Documents menus, Privacy, most states) and 11% CHANGED; a redraw would touch about 25 of 39 boards, cost two or more windows of agents on a 4-CPU box, and wait on the owner's re-approval, while the build must anyway keep the live control and restyle it from tokens. The parity Fix column already says exactly what each CHANGED/MISSING row needs, so the builder gets it inline in B<n>.md (DO NOT BUILD AS DRAWN flag) and the board is the look reference only. Safety nets: reviewer negative-twin tests per CHANGED row; label sweep. Optional and NON-BLOCKING: after B9 and after B13 a small parallel workflow may redraw only the boards whose decision the build overruled (EditorAts, EditorDraft, Jobs/JobsList/MobileJobs, ProjectBacklog, EditorTemplates), from screenshots of the built UI, so the canvas stays a faithful spec; skip it if the owner does not ask.
